questions.q: What is the article's central argument?
options: Climate risk drives multinationals away from poor countries, hurting both sides
Poor countries cause most emissions, so they should pay for adaptation
Foreign investment is largely unaffected by climate vulnerability
Companies should exit all risky markets and invest at home
questions.explain: Avoidance costs developing countries jobs and technology and costs firms opportunities.

questions.q: What broad finding do several studies, including the author's, report about foreign investment and climate vulnerability?
options: Foreign investment increases in more climate-vulnerable countries
Only small firms avoid climate-vulnerable markets while multinationals stay
Multinationals systematically avoid the most climate-vulnerable countries
Investment patterns are driven solely by trade agreements, not climate
questions.explain: Multiple studies, including the author's analysis, find that more climate-vulnerable countries received less foreign investment.

questions.q: Which company halted a $200 million data center in Chile?
options: Microsoft
Google
Toyota
questions.explain: Google halted its plans after an environmental court revoked its permit.

questions.q: Which are named as examples of countries supplying critical minerals while highly climate-vulnerable?
options: Chile and Kenya, where data centers were halted
Vietnam and Thailand, hit by typhoons and floods
Mozambique and Nigeria, covered by World Bank insurance
Democratic Republic of Congo and Indonesia
questions.explain: DRC supplies most of the world's cobalt and Indonesia dominates nickel.

questions.q: Why does the author recommend better, more local risk data?
options: To let companies avoid only the riskiest areas, not whole countries
To justify banning new investment in any flood-prone region
To lower the foreign aid sent to climate-vulnerable countries
To replace insurance from international development banks
questions.explain: National scores hide local variation; finer data would limit avoidance to the riskiest sites.
